Hi Sara & Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Discovery recap: You want to evaluate Redwood for high-throughput inference across customer-facing features (chat + embeddings). Primary success metrics: token latency < 150ms p50, predictable monthly costs, and SOC2+data residency in US.
- Stakeholders you mentioned: Product (Sara), Procurement (Tom), Legal (TBD — please confirm), Security (TBD).

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Please confirm the economic buyer and Legal/Security points of contact (name + email + preferred contract sequencing).
2) Can you confirm preferred turn times for NDA / DPA / MSA reviews on your side? (we typically see NDA: 1-2 business days; DPA: 3-7; MSA: 3-10 depending on redlines)
3) We’ll prep our standard NDA and DPA templates and share via DocuSign for signature-first routing if that matches your flow.

Attachments I’ll share in the next email: Redwood NDA (fillable), Redwood DPA template, and a 1-page data flow diagram for your security team.

If it helps, Vivek (cc'd) will be available for a short security scoping call once we have your security contact. Dev (cc'd) will help with KMS/HSM and data residency questions.

Proposed: If you confirm stakeholders today, I’ll send the NDA over by EOD and we can start parallel security questionnaire work once NDA is signed.

Thanks —

Marissa Cole

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the recap — good summary. Confirming stakeholders on our side: 
- Economic buyer: Sara Li (Product) — sara.li@novahealth.com
- Procurement lead: Tom Barnes — tom.barnes@novahealth.com (that’s me)
- Legal (commercial contracts): Jennifer Shaw — j.shaw@novahealth.com (cc'd)
- Security: Aaron Kim (security@novahealth.com) — I’ll introduce separately if you need a direct thread.

Preferred sequencing on our side:
1) NDA first (we like to get mutual NDAs signed before documents are exchanged)
2) Security questionnaire + data flow diagram concurrently once NDA is in place
3) DPA review next (we typically request DPA redlines prior to final MSA if there are data residency/KMS requirements)
4) MSA last — commercial negotiation/terms after DPA scope confirmed

Typical internal turn times (estimate):
- NDA: 1-2 business days (we can usually sign quick)
- DPA: 5-7 business days for initial redlines
- MSA: 7-14 business days (may take longer if legal escalates on indemnity/SLA)

I’ve attached our security questionnaire and a short procurement checklist to speed review. Jennifer — feel free to add any notes on routing.

Tom
Director, Procurement | NovaHealth
tom.barnes@novahealth.com | (617) 555-2233

Thanks Tom — super helpful. Jennifer — great to have you looped. 

Per your sequencing and turn times, suggested Redwood routing (we can adjust to your preferences):
- Step 0: Mutual NDA (DocuSign) — sign first so Security questionnaire and any internal docs can flow.
- Step 1: Security questionnaire + 1-page data flow diagram (we’ll attach) — Vivek/Dev will be available for a 30-min review call once Aaron or your security lead is available.
- Step 2: DPA review — we’ll send our DPA template and can take your redlines. If your legal prefers, we can accept DPA redlines before finalizing MSA.
- Step 3: MSA / commercial terms — finalize after DPA scope confirmed; we can run a parallel commercial worksheet to shorten cycle.

Turn-time commitments from Redwood: NDA: same day EOD if received before 4pm PT; DPA: target 3 business days for initial response; MSA: target 5 business days for first pass (complex redlines may take longer). If your team needs accelerated SLA, we can commit to a timeline under a signed mutual NDA + procurement SOW.

I’m attaching our NDA and DPA templates for your review. I’ll send the DocuSign link for the NDA in a separate email this afternoon.

Hi all —

Thanks for the clear plan. A few notes from Legal: 
1) NDA: happy to sign mutual NDA — please send via DocuSign. We generally turnaround NDAs within 1 business day.
2) DPA: we’ll prioritize the DPA review after NDA; two redline items to flag up front: data residency (US-only), and KMS key management (we prefer customer-managed keys / HSM where available).
3) MSA: commercial terms are straightforward but we will want explicit SLA language and limitations of liability clarified.

Requested artifacts for our security review:
- 1-page data flow diagram (production + staging)
- KMS/HSM options and whether the platform supports customer-managed keys
- SOC2 report (redacted) and any penetration test summaries or attestations

I’ve attached our internal redline guide to help accelerate review and I can route internally for a faster turnaround if Vivek/Dev can answer the KMS/HSM and data-residency questions in the next 48 hours.

I’m available tomorrow morning (Fri) 9–11am ET for a 20–30 minute sync if that helps.

Jennifer Shaw
Sr. Counsel, Contracts | NovaHealth
j.shaw@novahealth.com | (617) 555-0199
